gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP reads tall and modern, its curves sweeping open instead of curling shut. And Quilon sits above it with a thick-thin rhythm that feels editorial, giving the sturdy body something to answer to.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Quilon's strokes swell and thin in a slow, commanding rhythm. Noto Sans Kannada follows in a gentle plain sans, its capitals rising only slightly and its s curves opening wide, so long paragraphs feel friendly and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Quilon's large open counters in tall a, e and s give it an editorial, commanding look, with moderate thick and thin strokes. Shrink it too far and that shading fades next to Noto Sans Kayah Li.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Quilon has mild stress, so every stroke stays solid and readable, and its slow ebb and flow carries the editorial weight. Noto Sans Kharoshthi does the quieter job, laying down a dark, steady stripe of lowercase with curves that never close.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Quilon gives its words a faint shimmer as the weight shifts, and its big counters in a, e and s feel editorial. Noto Sans Khmer stands proud beneath, nearly capital-sized.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Shaded, confident letters lead here, with Quilon's stroke thickness drifting gently through each word and its tall a, e and s opening wide. Noto Sans Khojki then offers exits that let light through, so keep the heading comfortably large.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi reads clean and approachable, with capitals and lowercase close in height and rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. But Quilon brings the weight variation, a modest, readable swell across every curve, and that gap is what the pair does best.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-kr: Quilon draws hairlines that stay fairly sturdy next to its stems, with a calm ebb and flow giving it editorial authority. Noto Sans KR settles in beside it as a plain sans, generous in its curve gaps and stubby in its ascenders next to a big x-height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lao: Quilon's bowls thin slightly at the sides, and its tall a, e and s give headings a commanding, editorial lift. Yet Noto Sans Lao rises even higher in its lowercase, with mouths that stay open, so the two meet at a lively height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Quilon is stencil-cut, with bar widths that vary mildly. Noto Sans Lao Looped is a plain sans whose words form solid blocks and whose bowls stay unfinished on one side, so extended reading moves along smoothly.
